title: Committee of Supply – Head K (Ministry of Education)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head K (Ministry of Education)

sections.label: OECD PISA disadvantaged students
sections.summary: The OECD's PISA study found Singapore students from less advantaged backgrounds outperformed international peers of similar backgrounds and beat the OECD average in all core domains.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: The Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD)'s Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA) study found that our students from less advantaged backgrounds not only outperformed their international counterparts of similar socioeconomic backgrounds, but they did better than the OECD average in all core domains.

sections.label: 97% in 2021
sections.summary: Today, about 97% did so in the year 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Today, about 97% did so in the year 2021.

sections.label: MOE Kindergartens and preschool places
sections.summary: There are 50 MOE Kindergartens today, and the 60 MKs will contribute to achieving 80% Government-supported preschool places by around 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Today, there are 50 MOE Kindergartens (MKs) all over Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: The 60 MKs will contribute to the Government's commitment to achieve 80% Government-supported preschool places by around 2025.

sections.label: Primary school choice
sections.summary: Each year, about 98% of Singaporean children get into a primary school of their choice or within two kilometres of their residence.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Each year, about 98% of Singaporean children get into a primary school of their choice, or within two kilometres of their residence.

sections.label: PSLE scoring system changes
sections.summary: MOE introduced changes to the PSLE scoring system in 2021 so results are less finely differentiated and reflect students' objective performance rather than relative to peers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Instead, we should help them maximise their potential and do justice to their gifts.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: This is why MOE introduced changes to the PSLE scoring system in 2021, so that the results are no longer as finely differentiated and reflect students' objective performance, rather than relative to their peers.

sections.label: Removal of assessments and exams
sections.summary: All weighted assessments were removed for Primary 1 and Primary 2 since 2019, and Mid-Year Examinations will be removed for all primary and secondary levels this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Indeed, we have been focusing more on important life skills in our curriculum.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Hence, all weighted assessments have been removed for Primary 1 and Primary 2 since 2019, and Mid-Year Examinations will be removed for all primary and secondary levels this year.

sections.label: PSLE as checkpoint
sections.summary: Removing the PSLE would lose a checkpoint for assessing students' mastery of core concepts when moving from primary to secondary school.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: First, if we do away with the PSLE, we lose an important checkpoint in assessing a student's mastery of core concepts as they transit from primary to secondary school.

sections.label: Full Subject-Based Banding implementation
sections.summary: Next year will mark a milestone with the implementation of Full Subject-Based Banding in the secondary education system.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Next year will mark a significant milestone with the implementation of Full Subject-Based Banding (FSBB) in our secondary education system.

sections.label: Posting Groups for Secondary 1
sections.summary: From the 2024 Secondary 1 cohort, MOE will post Primary 6 students through three Posting Groups mapped to PSLE score ranges for Normal (Technical), Normal (Academic) and Express courses.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Starting from the 2024 Secondary 1 cohort, MOE will post Primary 6 students to secondary schools through three Posting Groups – Posting Groups 1, 2, and 3 – mapped to the PSLE score ranges for Normal (Technical), Normal (Academic) and Express courses respectively.

sections.label: SEC replacing O and N Levels
sections.summary: Starting from 2027, SEC will replace the separate Singapore-Cambridge GCE O and N Level examinations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Starting from 2027, SEC will replace the separate Singapore-Cambridge General Certificate of Education (GCE) "O" and "N" Level examinations.

sections.label: Expanded IHL admission pathways
sections.summary: FSBB changes will be accompanied by expanded admission and progression pathways in Institutes of Higher Learning to cater to a wider profile of students.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: To cater to a wider profile of students offering subjects at different subject levels, FSBB changes will be accompanied by expanded admission and progression pathways in our Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs).

sections.label: PW as Pass/Fail subject
sections.summary: PW will be made a Pass/Fail subject and excluded from the computation of the University Admission Score.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: To encourage students to make the most of the exciting collaborative and interdisciplinary learning experience offered by PW, we will make it a Pass/Fail subject, and exclude it from the computation of the University Admission Score (UAS).

sections.label: PW requirement for university admission
sections.summary: A Pass in PW remains required for admission to Autonomous Universities, implemented from Academic Year 2024 for the JC1 and MI Year 2 cohort.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: A Pass in PW will still be required for admission to the Autonomous Universities (AUs), to show that students have attained the skills which are critical for future learning and work.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: We will implement these changes from the Academic Year 2024, the JC1 and Millenia Institute (MI) Year 2 cohort onwards.

sections.label: Fourth content-based subject UAS
sections.summary: From Academic Year 2026 admissions, the fourth content-based subject will not count in UAS by default, only if it improves UAS.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: From the Academic Year 2026 admissions, the fourth content-based subject will no longer be counted in the computation of UAS by default and will only be included if it improves UAS.

sections.label: Removal of Mid-Year Examinations
sections.summary: Mid-Year Examinations will be removed for all junior colleges and Millenia Institute, similar to primary and secondary schools.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Lastly, similar to what has already been done for our primary and secondary schools, we will remove Mid-Year Examinations for all junior colleges and MI.

sections.label: Enrolment in stackable courses
sections.summary: Annual enrolment into stackable courses grew from around 31,000 to around 36,000 between 2018 and 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Over the past few years, annual enrolment into stackable courses has grown from around 31,000 to around 36,000, from 2018 to 2022.

sections.label: Lifetime cohort participation rate increase
sections.summary: The lifetime cohort participation rate for publicly funded university degrees will increase by 10 percentage points, from 50% to 60% by 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: In close consultation with the Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI), Ministry of Manpower (MOM) and economic agencies, we have decided to increase the "lifetime cohort participation rate" for publicly funded university degrees by 10 percentage points, from 50% currently to 60% by 2025, so that more Singaporeans can obtain a degree from our AUs, not just at the point of 18 years old, but throughout their life.

sections.label: Post-Diplomas credit exemptions
sections.summary: Polytechnics' Post-Diplomas will be recognised for credit exemptions, providing a more seamless upgrading pathway for Diploma holders.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Polytechnics' Post-Diplomas will also be recognised for credit exemptions, to provide a more seamless upgrading pathway for Diploma holders.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Credit top-up support
sections.summary: Support is being considered through a SkillsFuture Credit top-up and training allowances for mid-careerists in intensive full-time training.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: For example, we are considering how to provide more support through a SkillsFuture Credit top-up, and training allowances for mid-careerists in transition who go for intensive full-time training.

sections.label: MTL speech tools for students
sections.summary: MTL Text-to-Speech and Speech Evaluation tools let students practise oral communication and receive instant feedback.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: First, with the MTL Text-to-Speech and Speech Evaluation tools, students can practise their oral communication skills and receive feedback instantly.

sections.label: AI systems for educators
sections.summary: MOE will introduce AI-enabled systems to help educators teach more effectively, implemented through SLS from the fourth quarter this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: In the next phase, MOE will also introduce AI-enabled systems to better support our educators to teach more effectively.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: MOE will progressively implement these systems through the SLS from the fourth quarter this year.

sections.label: Refreshing Teacher Growth Model
sections.summary: MOE is refreshing the Teacher Growth Model to help teachers plan personal and professional development.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: To help teachers plan for their personal and professional development, MOE is refreshing the Teacher Growth Model.

sections.label: Compulsory internships at IHLs
sections.summary: Polytechnics, ITE and most AUs made internships compulsory, with over 2,300 companies partnering IHLs last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: All polytechnics, ITE and most AUs have made internships a compulsory component of their courses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Last year, more than 2,300 companies partnered our IHLs to provide internships.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The students were able to connect what they had learnt in the classroom to their workplace, while the companies were able to access a new pipeline of talent.

sections.label: UCN rollout to more towns
sections.summary: UCN collaboration with social service agencies supports plans to roll out to 12 more towns in 2023, supporting about 1,300 students and families.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Schools similarly appreciate that closer collaboration with social service agencies (SSAs) from the UCN support.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: This gives us the confidence to continue with our plans to roll out the UCN nationwide to 12 more towns in 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: We expect to support about 1,300 students and their families this year.

sections.label: School initiative expansion
sections.summary: Schools supported under this initiative grew from 23 in 2019 to 47 in 2022, with plans to expand to about 100 schools.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: The number of schools supported under this initiative has grown from 23 schools in 2019 to 47 schools in 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: We plan to further expand this to about 100 schools in the next few years, to support about 13,000 students.

sections.label: Financial assistance and bursaries
sections.summary: Financial assistance and bursary provisions were recently enhanced for Singapore Citizen students from lower-income households in schools and IHLs.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: For example, we recently enhanced financial assistance and bursary provisions for Singapore Citizens (SC) students from lower-income households in our schools and our IHLs respectively.

sections.label: Non-citizen student assistance
sections.summary: Non-citizen students with financial difficulties can approach their schools for assistance.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Non-citizen students with financial difficulties can approach their schools for assistance.

sections.label: Edusave and private school eligibility
sections.summary: All Singapore Citizens aged seven to 16 receive yearly Edusave contributions, but students in private schools including madrasahs are not eligible for MOE financial assistance and Edusave awards.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: All SCs, aged seven to 16, receive yearly Edusave contributions for their educational uses.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: However, students in private schools, including those in madrasahs, are not eligible for MOE's financial assistance scheme and Edusave awards.

sections.label: Special Education school accessibility
sections.summary: Accessibility to quality SPED schools was enhanced for students with moderate to severe SEN, and a fifth SPED school for Autism Spectrum Disorder was announced.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: For students with moderate to severe SEN, we have enhanced accessibility to quality Special Education (SPED) schools by strengthening curriculum efforts and ensuring sufficient capacity to cater to different disability profiles.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: We recently announced a fifth SPED school for students with Autism Spectrum Disorder who can access the national curriculum.

sections.label: School Partnerships replacing Satellite Partnerships
sections.summary: From 2023, Satellite Partnerships will be replaced by School Partnerships between Gen Ed schools and SPED schools to broaden and deepen existing partnerships.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: From 2023, Satellite Partnerships will be replaced by School Partnerships, that is, partnership between Gen Ed schools and SPED schools, to broaden and deepen existing partnerships while cultivating stronger and more collaboration between SPED schools and Gen Ed schools.

sections.label: SPED syllabuses launched
sections.summary: Three SPED syllabuses were launched in the past two years, and two more will be launched this year.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Three SPED syllabuses were launched in the past two years for the learning domains which include one, Visual Arts; two, Daily Living Skills; and three, Vocational Education.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Two additional SPED syllabuses in one, Communication and Language; and two, Social-Emotional Learning will be launched this year.

sections.label: SPED funding and exit age
sections.summary: The exit age remains 18, while MOE has extended funding for SPED students who can offer vocational certification.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: While the exit age remains at 18 years old, MOE has extended funding for SPED students who can offer vocational certification.

sections.label: Refreshed CCE curriculum roll-out
sections.summary: The roll-out for the refreshed CCE curriculum started in 2021 and will be completed by this year.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: The roll-out for the refreshed CCE curriculum started in 2021 and will be completed by this year.

sections.label: Student well-being and counsellors
sections.summary: Schools set aside time each term for student well-being, and efforts to recruit school counsellors have been stepped up.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Schools have also set aside dedicated time and space at the start of each term for teachers to engage students on issues affecting their well-being.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: We have also stepped up efforts in the recruitment of school counsellors and will continue to grow our pool of teacher-counsellors.

sections.label: Enhanced ITE curricular structure
sections.summary: ITE introduced the enhanced three-year curricular structure leading directly to a Higher Nitec from the 2022 intake.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: First, to enhance students' career readiness and aspirations, ITE introduced the enhanced three-year ITE curricular structure leading directly to a Higher Nitec from the 2022 intake.

sections.label: ITE curricular transition timeline
sections.summary: ITE will monitor the first phase's outcomes and is on track to transition remaining courses by 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: ITE will continue to monitor the outcomes of the first phase of implementation closely.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: It is on track in transitioning the remaining courses to the enhanced curricular structure by 2026.

sections.label: PFP access expansion
sections.summary: PFP access will expand to G3 and mixed G3-G2 students from the 2028 intake, with yearly intake possibly rising to 2,600.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: To allow a wider learner profile to benefit from the PFP, access to the PFP will be expanded to include students taking G3 subjects or a mix of G3 and G2 level subjects.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: This change will take place from the 2028 PFP intake and the number of students accepted every year could increase up to 2,600 from about 1,700 today.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: The PFP admissions criteria will be maintained to ensure that students continue to have the fundamentals to cope with the rigour of the PFP.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: We will also adopt a cluster-based admissions approach for the PFP from the 2026 intake.

sections.label: New ITE WSDip programmes
sections.summary: In 2023, ITE will launch four new WSDip programmes, bringing the total to 40 under the WSDips initiative.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: In 2023, ITE will expand its WSDip offering by launching four new programmes, bringing together a total to 40 programmes under the WSDips initiative.

sections.label: Removal of secondary streams
sections.summary: The Express, Normal (Academic) and Normal (Technical) streams will be removed following the implementation of Full Subject-Based Banding.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Arising from the implementation of the Full Subject-Based Banding (FSBB), the Express, Normal (Academic) and Normal (Technical) streams will be removed.

sections.label: PFP opened to more profiles
sections.summary: From the 2028 Polytechnic intake, the PFP, now limited to Normal (Academic) students, will be opened to more learner profiles.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Beginning with the 2028 Polytechnic intake, the Polytechnic Foundation Programme (PFP), which is limited to students in the Normal (Academic) stream today, will be opened further to more learner profiles.

sections.label: WSDips and TDs outcomes
sections.summary: The WSDips and TDs expansion supports ITE students seeking diplomas, with 1,600 students having passed and obtained good jobs.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: The expansion of the WSDips and TDs programmes aims to support ITE students in their aspirations for upgrading and to acquire Diploma qualification.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: So far, 1,600 ITE students have passed the WSDips and TDs diploma courses and managed to get good jobs with salaries equivalent to our polytechnic graduates.

sections.label: Kembara Nusantara programme launch
sections.summary: The Malay Language Learning and Promotion Committee collaborated with the Mandai Wildlife Group to launch the Kembara Nusantara programme.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: For example, the Malay Language Learning and Promotion Committee (MLLPC) collaborated with the Mandai Wildlife Group to launch the Kembara Nusantara programme.

sections.label: Through-train programme selection at Primary 1
sections.summary: The passage questions who gets to go to the through-train programme, noting it is difficult to know children's abilities and interests at Primary 1.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: First, who gets to go to the through-train programme?

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: I think most of us as parents will know, at Primary 1, it is very difficult, if not impossible, for us to know the abilities and interests of our children.

sections.label: Checkpoints and resourcing schools
sections.summary: The passage asks how students get into the correct educational setting without checkpoints, and how schools are resourced with full programmes and pathways.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The third issue: if we have no checkpoint at P6 or any other years – you can argue whether it is P6 or any other time – if you have no checkpoints at all, then how do we help our students to get into the correct educational setting?

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Which then comes to the fifth issue: how do we resource these schools with a complete suite of programmes for the students that we have taken in at P1 with the promise that regardless of their abilities, after they have gone through it for various years, that we will be able to provide them with the full pathways?

sections.label: Through-train programme experience not uniformly positive
sections.summary: The passage states that some systems have segments with the through-train programme and the experience has not been uniformly positive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Some of them have some segments of their system with this through-train programme and the experience has not been uniformly positive for the reasons that I mentioned.

sections.label: Polytechnic criterion and G2 subjects
sections.summary: The passage states that most polytechnics currently use a criterion equivalent to the Express stream, and that allowing G2 subjects is being considered.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: Today, for most polytechnics, the current criterion is equivalent to the Express stream – the five G3-dominant combination.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: As I mentioned in my speech earlier, we are considering allowing the usage of the G2 subjects.

sections.label: Pathways for G1, G2, G3 combinations
sections.summary: The passage states that for G1, G2 or G3 subject combinations there will be a pathway, including ITE, Higher NITEC, polytechnics, technical diploma or work-study.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: What we want to ensure is whether you do a subject at G1, G2 or G3, such a combination, there will be a pathway for you – it could be at our ITE, where, as I announced also, we now have the three-year Higher NITEC curriculum that they can aspire towards.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: And if that continues, then they can aspire towards joining the polytechnics afterwards, or joining our technical diploma programme or our work-study programme.

sections.label: IT firms hiring polytechnic and ITE students
sections.summary: The passage states that many IT industry firms ask for graduate degrees, and suggests they look at polytechnic and ITE students for certain jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Talk to them, inspire them, share with them what kind of skillsets are required and, at the same time, see what our students are capable of.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: But today, many of the IT industry firms want to ask for graduate degrees	 or IT-related graduate degrees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: So, we suggested to them, "Why don't you come and look at the polytechnic students and look at even the ITE students?" They can do certain jobs with their skill sets.

sections.label: Curriculum, industry training, adult skills
sections.summary: The passage states that partnership is needed to update curriculum and train workers, and that success covers workers' achievements beyond school.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: But it does require a partnership for us to keep ourselves updated in our curriculum so that we are at a faster speed to market, and it does require us to also work with the industry to keep training our workers so that they remain current even after they join the industry.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: And to Ms Denise Phua's question, today, if you look at the PISA score, at the school level, once they depart school, we are at the top of the league.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Today, we are not top of the league for the older age groups because our education system started a bit behind the other more established economies, but we have every aim to make sure that the skills of our adult workers remain at the top of their league in their respective age groups.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: And this is why our definition of success cannot be the first 15 years of what our children achieve in school, but the next 50 years of what our workers achieve beyond school.

sections.label: Skills frameworks for sectors
sections.summary: The passage states that SSG has been developing skills frameworks for different sectors, with 34 altogether for different industries.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: Indeed, it is a science; there is language around how skills should be defined.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: That is why for some time SSG  has been developing skills frameworks that apply to different sectors.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: There are altogether 34 now for different industries.

sections.label: Criteria for streamlining training providers
sections.summary: The passage states that streamlining criteria look at employment outcomes and whether training providers connect trainees with potential hirers and companies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: Coming to Ms Foo Mee Har's questions, on the criteria for streamlining training providers, it is quite challenging indeed because every training provider tells us they are very good in the courses that they are providing.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: So, what we do really is, we look at the employment outcomes, whether people who attend the courses get a job within a certain number of months after course completion, whether the training providers are able to connect the trainees or the course participants with potential hirers and companies out there so that the chances and the networking opportunities for the trainees would be much better.

sections.label: Continuing Education and Training Centres
sections.summary: The passage states that there are Continuing Education and Training (CET) Centres, about 20 of them now.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: In fact, we have Continuing Education and Training (CET) Centres.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: I think there are about 20 of them now.

sections.label: Explaining societal considerations
sections.summary: The passage states that the speaker will explain what is meant by societal considerations, answering clarifications by Mr Louis Chua.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Chair, let me explain what I mean by societal considerations, to answer both of the clarifications by Mr Louis Chua.

sections.label: Home-school distance question
sections.summary: The passage asks whether just using home-school distance alone will solve this problem.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Will just using home-school distance alone solve this problem?

sections.label: Device and school access support
sections.summary: Free dongles and continued school access are provided to students facing data or home difficulties, regardless of financial background.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: First, when we distributed the devices to our schools and the students, for those who are unable or have difficulties with the data charges, we provided them with free dongles for them to access the data.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Second, for those who have difficulties with their home environment, which may be less than conducive, we continue to open our schools and allow the students to access the school services, even in the depth of the COVID-19 crisis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: We will continue to provide such access to all students, regardless of their financial background.

sections.label: Through-train system and school choice
sections.summary: The speaker thanks Ms Denise Phua for ideas on the through-train system and says stresses of secondary school choice are already reduced for a segment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Chairman, we thank Ms Denise Phua for offering us her ideas and help, to think through and step through some of those issues about the through-train system that we talked about.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: I just want to say this, short of doing that today, for a certain segment of our population, we essentially have already reduced the stresses that are associated with school choice when you go to secondary school.

sections.label: MK, NIEC and examination load
sections.summary: MK and NIEC help determine baselines, share best practices, set subsidies, and cluster-level exam setting could lighten teachers' load.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Setting up MK together with the National Institute of Early Childhood Development (NIEC) has been most instrumental in helping us to determine this baseline, where we can share the best practices with the rest of the other preschool providers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The second very useful thing when we started MK was this: now that we have a better understanding and grasp of the cost drivers for any preschool education, that allows us to determine the subsidies that we should be giving to the various preschools to make sure that the essentials are fulfilled and not frittered away on other things, which are, perhaps optional, perhaps frills.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Currently, I think a lot of teachers and educators, particularly in primary schools and secondary schools, are very bogged down with setting examination scripts – every year, year on year, trying to innovate and find new ways to ask questions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: And to lighten the load, can we do it at the cluster level for economies of scale?

sections.label: Sharing best practices 80/20 rule
sections.summary: Educators are encouraged to share best practices, with 80% shared and 20% customised to local students' needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: In fact, I encourage all my educators to try to share their best practices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: I have what I call the "80/20" rule.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: For 80%, you can share, download the best practices from everywhere.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: But for every teacher, you must have 20% where you customise to the local needs of the students in your school because the learning profiles of students in the different schools are quite different.

sections.label: White space in Teachers Growth Model
sections.summary: White space in the Teachers Growth Model means intentionally setting aside time for teachers to develop skills and competencies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: White space to MOE, in the Teachers Growth Model (TGM) means intentionally setting aside time for teachers to develop their skills and competencies.

sections.label: Higher Nitec student and lecturer demands
sections.summary: Since Higher Nitec began in 2022, students and lecturers face added demands, with about 20 weekly classroom hours and 40 students per lecturer.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: So, with the introduction of a Higher Nitec since 2022, both the students and the lecturers have to grapple with additional demands.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I understand that each student has about 20 hours of classroom time every week, and each lecturer has to handle 40 students, which include the SEN ones.

sections.label: ITE Higher Nitec flexible completion
sections.summary: ITE students who complete their internship may leave after two years, work, and return to finish their Higher Nitec modules.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: For the ITE, yes, Mr Don Wee highlighted that we have the three-year Higher Nitec curriculum now, but we do acknowledge that some students may take a longer time and they may want to take some time off after two years.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: As long as they have done their internship, they can leave ITE for a while, continue to work, if they are ready to work and come back and continue to stack up their modules and then complete their Higher Nitec and subsequently go on.

sections.label: SEN support and case management
sections.summary: More SEN-trained officers are provided, and ITE is being piloted with an integrated case management framework with added staff.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: With regards to SEN, we are giving them more SEN-trained officers to help them because we do want our SEN students who were from our mainstream schools to continue to move on to our Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs).

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: We are also looking at piloting at the ITE what we call an integrated case management framework, where we will augment the ITEs with staff to help them coordinate support services required by students with higher needs.

sections.label: MOE expanded scope of work
sections.summary: MOE now does more from preschool through primary, secondary, beyond secondary and CET, with much work remaining.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: MOE is doing so much more now from preschool, to primary, secondary, beyond secondary, now even CET, so the 15 plus 50, and really, there is a lot of work to be done.

sections.label: Better career guidance, CET, recognition
sections.summary: Three goals are set: better career guidance through coaching, better access to quality CET, and better employer recognition of skills.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: First, better career guidance for youth who have just left school and new entrants into the workforce through career coaching.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Second, better access to quality Continuing Education and Training, also known as CET.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Third, better recognition of skills and competencies by employers.

sections.label: Training leave for workers
sections.summary: The submission proposes requiring employers to provide training leave for workers to undergo training and skills upgrading.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: In the same vein, I further submit that we should require employers to provide training leave for workers to undergo training and skills upgrading.

sections.label: Rewarding CET learners, employer training
sections.summary: Learners developing via CET should be rewarded, employers should use training opportunities, and better guidance, CET access, recognition and training leave are needed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Instead of an unhealthy overemphasis on academic qualifications, we should reward learners who continuously develop themselves via CET programmes and modular courses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Employers, likewise, should also take the opportunity to leverage training opportunities, such as those offered by our NTUC's Training and Placement ecosystem, to train and develop workers thus strengthening their own talent pipeline.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: However, I am optimistic that we are moving in the right direction and we can achieve this with concerted effort from Government and society.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: We need to have better career guidance and coaching, better access to quality CET and better recognition of skills and competencies by employers and training leave to do all these.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Ultimately, both the learners and society will benefit when our workforce is equipped with the skills needed for a changing labour market.

sections.label: Alternate school admission and hiring
sections.summary: Speaker urges MOE to develop alternatives to exam-grade-based school admission and hiring, and to support alternate education school models.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Next, I wish to offer three suggestions today for MOE's consideration.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I urge the Ministry to research and develop an alternate system to the current (a) school admission and (b) staff recruitment system by employers for example, which predominantly uses exam grades and paper qualifications as the proxy for competencies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: We already know of tech companies and creative industries which prioritise portfolios, evidence of desired skills and experience over school results and use these for hiring decisions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I urge the Ministry to allow for and support the blooming of alternate education school models.

sections.label: Uplifting at-risk mid-career Singaporeans
sections.summary: Speaker urges the Ministry to study a segment of mid-career and middle-aged Singaporeans and develop programmes to uplift those at risk.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: So, let us be bold and take some calculated risks.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I urge the Ministry to conduct a deep study of a specific segment of mid-career and middle-aged Singaporeans and develop programmes to uplift those at risk.

sections.label: PIAAC literacy and numeracy results
sections.summary: The 2016 PIAAC report shows Singapore adults aged 16 to 34 fare well while those aged 45 to 65 scored below the OECD average in literacy and numeracy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The last PIAAC report was published in 2016.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: It shows that while Singapore adults aged 16 to 34 fare well, our older adults aged 45 to 65 performed lower than the OECD average in literacy and numeracy.

sections.label: Nature-based learning in schools
sections.summary: Speaker urges MOE to make outdoor and nature-based learning the main approach in early and primary education so all children benefit.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Nature provides the best classroom for such learning and all schools should be enabled to harness nature-based learning so that all children can benefit and not just those whose parents can afford private preschools.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I urge MOE to make outdoor and nature-based learning the main approach in early and primary education.

sections.label: Piloting naturalistic pedagogy curriculum
sections.summary: Speaker proposes training educators in naturalistic pedagogy, piloting a pre- and primary school curriculum in closed schools, and a longitudinal study from age three to 16.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Incorporating more play also imbues joy and helps foster stronger desire to deepen their pursuit of knowledge as they mature into tertiary years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We can begin by sending interested educators to receive training in naturalistic pedagogy and pioneer a detailed curriculum for pre- and primary school.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: To begin this transition, schools planned to be closed due to low demand can be re-designed to pilot this model.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Coupled with a longitudinal study of a cohort of children from age three to 16, the improvements to well-being and learning are observed along the way, MOE can scale the pilot to offer more spaces to willing parents progressively until it is accepted by most.

sections.label: Piloting through-train bypassing PSLE
sections.summary: Quoting Everychild.sg's White Paper, the speaker urges MOE to consider piloting a through-train primary and secondary programme that bypasses the PSLE.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Allow me to quote extracts from Everychild.sg's White Paper developed by Singaporean parents: "…the cultural norm among many Singaporean families is for a parent … to plan to take time off during the child's PSLE year, rather than during the first 1 – 2 years of the child's life… many Singaporean parents … prioritising giving their child undivided attention at the age of 11/12, which appears to the child to be tied to performance expectations, rather than the more unconditional and intimate love of infancy and early childhood.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We would be naive to think this does not have a negative impact on children's mental health, emotional development, self-esteem and future relationships." This is the third time I am urging MOE to consider piloting a through-train programme for primary and secondary school students, bypassing the PSLE and I have no intention of stopping.

sections.label: Refurbishing abandoned schools for pilot
sections.summary: The passage asks whether abandoned old school buildings can be refurbished into a couple of small schools for a pilot programme.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Can we not refurbish old school buildings that have been left abandoned for years, to a couple of small schools for a pilot programme?

sections.label: Compulsory scheme versus student-initiated learning
sections.summary: The passage supports self-directed learning but says making the scheme compulsory contradicts student-initiated learning and asks for an opt-out.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I am fully supportive of encouraging students to be more self-directed in their learning.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: However, I do feel that making this scheme compulsory is a contradiction to the whole idea of student-initiated learning.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Let students have a chance to opt out of the programme if it does not work for them.

sections.label: Optional test results in university admissions
sections.summary: The passage states studies of optional test results in university admissions show no change in application volume or yield rate but improved application diversity.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Studies of university admissions based on making test results optional reveal no evidence of changes in application volume or yield rate, but conversely, improvements in the diversity of applications.

sections.label: Workers' Party optional 10-year through-train
sections.summary: The passage states the Workers' Party proposal is an optional 10-year through-train programme from primary 1 through secondary 4 letting children bypass the PSLE.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The Workers' Party proposal is to introduce an optional 10-year through-train programme (10 YTS) from primary 1 through secondary 4 allows parents who wish to allow their children to bypass the PSLE to do so.

sections.label: Integrated Programme and 10 YTS tracks
sections.summary: The passage states the Integrated Programme lets secondary students skip O Levels for exams like A Levels, IB or high-school diploma, complementing non-10 YTS tracks.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The Integrated Programme (IP) already allows students in secondary schools to skip the "O" Levels and proceed directly to their ultimate high-school exam, such as the "A" Levels – Catholic High, Hwa Chong, Raffles Institution (RI), Victoria, St Nicholas, among others; the IB – Anglo-Chinese School (ACS) and St Joseph Institution (SJI); or the high-school diploma, which is the case for NUS High.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Importantly, this option will complement, but not replace, non-10 YTS tracks.

sections.label: Full SBB pilot and implementation
sections.summary: The passage states full SBB was piloted in 28 schools in 2020 and will be implemented in all secondary schools from 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
sentences.text: In 2020, full SBB was piloted in 28 schools and will be implemented in all secondary schools from 2024.

sections.label: Full subject-based banding resources
sections.summary: A major challenge of full subject-based banding is having resources for each band's specific needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
sentences.text: One of the major challenges of full subject-based banding is the availability of resources to cater to the specific needs of each band.

sections.label: Removal of mid-year examinations
sections.summary: Recent curriculum and assessment reviews led to removing mid-year examinations for all primary and secondary levels from 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
sentences.text: The recent reviews of curriculum content and assessment demand has led to the removal of mid-year examinations for all primary and secondary levels from 2023.

sections.label: Students' examination load
sections.summary: Within two years, students take two mid-year examinations, more promo and one prelims exam, plus common tests.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
sentences.text: Within two years, students have to take two mid-year examinations, more promo and one prelims exam, on top of their common tests.

sections.label: More JC direct school admission places
sections.summary: MOE announced more JC places for students entering through DSA, with non-Integrated Programme DSA places rising from 10% to 20%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David
sentences.text: In 2022, MOE announced that more places in junior colleges (JCs) will be made available for students entering with talents apart from their grades through the direct school admission (DSA) exercise from this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David
sentences.text: The number of DSA places for non-Integrated Programme students have also gone up from 10% to 20% of the yearly cohorts at Government and Government-aided JCs, including Anderson Serangoon JC, Eunoia JC and Victoria JC.

sections.label: Publishing diversity admission progress
sections.summary: The passage asks whether detailed annual information on progress towards admitting students from more diverse backgrounds can be published.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Could we therefore start to publish detailed information annually on the progress made towards admitting students from a more diverse background, so that we know if our efforts are paying off?

sections.label: South Korea educational broadcasting lectures
sections.summary: South Korea's Educational Broadcasting System holds accessible lectures for high school students, estimated to have cut private tutoring spending by 816 billion won in 2011.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: We should also take a leaf out of the book of heavily-tutored countries like South Korea, whose Educational Broadcasting System holds highly accessible lectures for high school students preparing for university admissions examinations.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: It was estimated that this service significantly reduced spending on private tutoring by 816 billion won back in 2011.

sections.label: Primary school priority schemes distance limit
sections.summary: MOE can keep the current priority schemes, but pupils admitted under them should face a 1- or 2-kilometre distance limit to the school.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: MOE can maintain the priority scheme under the current Phase 1, 2, 2A, 2B and 2C.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: But pupils admitted to the primary school under any of the above priority schemes, should be subject to a 1- or 2-kilometre distance limit to the school.

sections.label: P1 registration Phase 2C places
sections.summary: MOE tweaked the P1 registration framework by doubling places reserved in each school under Phase 2C from 2022 onwards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This has to start with our children and with our primary schools where social mixing has arguably been on the decline.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I was heartened by MOE's to tweak the Primary 1 (P1) registration framework by doubling the number of places reserved in each school under Phase 2C 2022 onwards.

sections.label: Citizenship and home-school distance allocation
sections.summary: The speaker suggested in 2021 using citizenship and home-school distance to allocate P1 vacancies across all three phases, retaining Phase 2A and 2B balloting criteria.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Since MOE recognises that going to a school nearby is in the educational interest of each child, as the Ministry has really made clear in its news release, then the P1 registration framework should be redesigned to make sure that we honour this commitment to every Singaporean child entering Primary 1.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This was why I suggested in 2021 that MOE should consider using citizenship and home-school distance as a primary means of allocating vacancies for all three phases of the P1 registration, while retaining the existing Phase 2A and 2B criteria for determining balloting priority.

sections.label: P1 registration complexity and Edusave eligibility
sections.summary: A CNA video questioned whether the P1 registration process perpetuates inequalities, and madrasah students are not eligible for the Edusave Award.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: CNA also recently broadcast a very thought-through talking point video which questioned If a complex and confusing P1 registration process actually perpetuates educational inequalities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: We can and we must take bolder steps to simplify the P1 registration framework and make it truly accessible for all.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: MOE's Edusave Award is a recognition to Singaporean students who have demonstrated good character, leadership, conduct, learning disposition and academic performance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, I note that Singaporean students who are studying in the full-time madrasahs are not eligible for the Edusave Award.

sections.label: Madrasah students Edusave Award eligibility
sections.summary: Full-time madrasah students excelling in non-religious subjects should be eligible for MOE's Edusave Award like public school students.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Separately, full-time madrasah students excelling in non-religious subject should be eligible for MOE's Edusave Award like Singaporean students in public schools.

sections.label: Extending FAS to all Singaporeans
sections.summary: The speaker proposes MOE extend the FAS to all Singaporean students who need it, regardless of institution type.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Nonetheless, as part of our ongoing efforts in making our society more inclusive, I would like to propose that MOE extends the FAS to all Singaporeans students who need it, regardless of the type of institution they are attending.

sections.label: Student wellbeing in schools and IHLs
sections.summary: The passage asks the Ministry to update on efforts promoting and supporting student wellbeing in schools and IHLs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Could the Ministry please update on its efforts in promoting and supporting the wellbeing for our students in schools and IHLs?

sections.label: Stress and grade worry surveys
sections.summary: The passage cites a 2022 Rakuten Insight survey and a 2017 OECD study on stress, anxiety and worry about grades.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: According to a survey by Rakuten Insight in Singapore in May 2022, 63% of those aged 16 to 24 had a higher level of stress or anxiety for the past 12 months, the highest of any age group.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: A 2017 OECD study found that 66% of students across all OECD countries said they were worried about poor grades at school but in Singapore, among Singaporean students, it was far higher at 86%.

sections.label: Korean system use in 2011
sections.summary: The passage states that in 2011, 3.9 million Koreans used the system, reducing private tutoring spending by about S$870 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In 2011, 3.9 million Koreans used the system, reducing private tutoring spending by about S$870 million.

sections.label: Expanding the PFP scheme
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Minister would consider expanding the PFP scheme given concerns over diverging employment outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Given this success and in light of concerns over the diverging employment outcomes of ITE versus polytechnic and university graduates, could the Minister consider expanding the PFP scheme to allow more students to benefit?

sections.label: MOE EdTech Plan and AI Singapore
sections.summary: The passage states that MOE's EdTech Plan guides a technology-enriched school environment and AI Singapore aims to build AI literacy and EdTech.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David
sentences.text: Currently, MOE's EdTech Plan guides the development of a technology-enriched school environment for teaching and learning.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David
sentences.text: On the education front, AI Singapore aims to build national literacy in AI and develop EdTech through working with various classroom stakeholders and partners.

sections.label: Reducing school curriculum
sections.summary: The passage says MOE should consider reducing school curriculum so students enjoy learning for knowledge rather than exams or grades.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
sentences.text: MOE should consider reducing school curriculum so that students will enjoy learning in order to acquire knowledge rather than learning to pass exams or to gain good grades.

sections.label: AI in teaching and learning
sections.summary: Speaker asks what efforts the Ministry made to support integrating technology, including AI, into teaching and learning, and declares a Tasek Jurong role.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
sentences.text: Teach them the skills to discern, to edit, to incorporate critical thinking to the original AI solution.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
sentences.text: Thus, I would like to ask the Minister what efforts the Ministry made to support the integration of technology, including AI, into teaching and learning practices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, I would like to declare that I am the founding director and board member of Tasek Jurong Limited, a charity and Institution of Public Character (IPC) for disadvantaged youths and Singaporeans.

sections.label: SkillsFuture courses and PwDs
sections.summary: The Disabled People's Association says PwDs encountered SkillsFuture-funded courses using charts and diagrams with no text descriptions, difficult for visually-impaired persons.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: According to the Disabled People's Association, PwDs have encountered SkillsFuture-funded courses that use charts and diagrams with no text descriptions, creating difficulties for visually-impaired persons.

sections.label: Accessibility of SkillsFuture courses
sections.summary: Speaker asks what proportion of SkillsFuture courses are accessible to PwDs and how SSG ensures accessibility and standardisation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Can I ask the Minister what proportion of SkillsFuture courses are currently accessible to PwDs?

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: How is SSG ensuring that most SkillsFuture courses are accessible and will there be a standardisation of accessibility in all SkillsFuture courses?

sections.label: Support for SEN students
sections.summary: Speaker says there have been meaningful developments in identifying needs, making referrals and providing support to SEN students in mainstream and special education schools.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: In particular, within the school setting, there have been meaningful developments in identifying needs, making the appropriate referrals and providing support to students with special educational needs within the mainstream schools and the special education schools.

sections.label: Independent living and SEN sectors
sections.summary: Speaker says students must be equipped with skills to live independently and asks whether there is a plan for sectors SEN students could enter and excel in.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: At the basic level, we need to ensure that they are equipped with the necessary skills to be able to live as independently as possible and navigate through life.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Additionally, do we also have a plan as to which sectors in the future students with SEN could possibly enter and excel in?

sections.label: Special needs educators' profession
sections.summary: Speaker says special needs educators are committed and hopes the Ministry enhances the profession through progression pathways and improved remuneration.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I have met many special needs educators who are deeply committed to their work, go the extra mile to lookout for the students under their care and most importantly, they have a very big heart for the children.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I hope the Ministry continues to help enhance this profession by developing progression pathways and improving remuneration of the teachers in the special needs sector.

sections.label: SEN student educational outcomes
sections.summary: Educational outcomes for students with SEN in mainstream primary, secondary and post-secondary settings are currently inconsistent.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: The educational outcomes for students with SEN in mainstream schools however, primary, secondary and post-secondary settings are currently inconsistent.

sections.label: SPED school exit age
sections.summary: The speaker urges MOE to extend the formal SPED school exit age to 21 for all SPED schools, beyond the current age 18.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: To better support students in SPED schools, I urge MOE to: One, extend the formal SPED school exit age to age 21 for all SPED schools, beyond the current age 18.

sections.label: Teacher work hours guidelines
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether MOE can establish clearer guidelines on work hours and designated times for teachers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
sentences.text: First, could MOE establish clearer guidelines on work hours and designated times for teachers?

sections.label: Policy against teacher harassment
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether MOE can establish a zero-tolerance policy with clear protocols for handling harassment or abuse of teachers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
sentences.text: Third, could MOE establish a zero-tolerance policy with clear protocols for handling harassment or abuse of teachers?

sections.label: PEI education quality and approvals
sections.summary: The speaker asks MOE to share plans to improve PEI education quality and credibility, and how it will work with ICA and MOM on approvals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Given this, I would like to ask MOE to share its plans to improve the quality and credibility of education concerning PEIs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In addition, could MOE share how it plans to work with other Government agencies such as ICA and MOM to ensure necessary approvals such as student pass applications and training work pass applications are processed seamlessly?

sections.label: MOE support in Hong Kong
sections.summary: Minister of State Gan said MOE provides funding and teaching support to one international school in Hong Kong for Singaporean children's reintegration.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: In a response to a Parliamentary Question I filed late last year, Minister of State Gan explained that MOE already provides funding and teaching support to one international school in Hong Kong.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: She said that MOE did so because there were a sizable number of Singaporean children there and that this assistance helped with the reintegration of these kids back to our educational system here.

sections.label: Government SkillsFuture support sharpened
sections.summary: The Government has sharpened SkillsFuture support to prioritise skills needed for the future economy, including one-time top-up credit and additional credit for Mid-Career Support.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
sentences.text: Over the years, the Government has sharpened its support of SkillsFuture to prioritise the development of skills needed to be competitive in the future economy, as seen in the one-time top-up SkillsFuture credit and additional SkillsFuture credit for Mid-Career Support.

sections.label: Measuring SkillsFuture programme success
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Minister can share how the Government now measures the success of the SkillsFuture programme.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
sentences.text: Can the Minister share how the Government now measures the success of the SkillsFuture programme?

sections.label: Training programmes and skills frameworks
sections.summary: It provides training programmes for skills upgrading and mastery, with 34 industries currently having a defined skills framework.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay
sentences.text: It also provides training programmes for skills upgrading and mastery.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay
sentences.text: There are currently 34 industries with a defined skills framework.

sections.label: Statistics on Skills Framework adoption
sections.summary: The passage asks MOE for statistics on employer adoption of the Skills Framework in hiring and on Singaporeans gaining employment or progressing after training.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay
sentences.text: Given the above, I would like to ask MOE if there are any statistics on the actual adoption by the employers of the Skills Framework in hiring employees within the stated sector?

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay
sentences.text: Also, are there any statistics on how the Skills Framework has allowed Singaporeans to either gain employment or progress in their existing roles after undergoing training in these areas?

sections.label: Streamlining SSG WSQ course certification
sections.summary: The passage asks whether SSG would consider streamlining processes so a training institution can offer SSG/WSQ courses without separate certification applications.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay
sentences.text: As Singapore's economy develops rapidly and there is a need to ramp up capacity to allow Singaporeans to be trained, would SSG consider streamlining the processes that would enable a training institution to offer SSG/WSQ courses without having to apply for separate certifications?

sections.label: Evolving SkillsFuture quality and funding
sections.summary: The passage proposes evolving the SkillsFuture framework to differentiate training programmes and providers by quality standards, KPIs and funding, possibly along three categories.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: As we gear up to make training truly count, an important step is to evolve the SkillsFuture framework to clearly differentiate training programmes and training providers in terms of quality standards, key performance indicators (KPIs) and funding.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: For example, the Government may consider differentiating training programmes along three broad categories for better targeting and funding model.

sections.label: SkillsFuture training provider funding review
sections.summary: The Government should review SkillsFuture training provider funding to foster capability development, quality standards and impactful learning outcomes, selecting LTPs for scale and industry-tailored programmes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: The Government should review the funding model for training providers under SkillsFuture to foster capability development, quality standards and impactful learning outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Rather than having a plethora of small players, LTPs should be selected based on their commitment to build scale and capabilities to deliver a full suite of training programmes tailored to the industry.

sections.label: Adult learning quality initiatives
sections.summary: IAL leads the Innovative Learning 2.0 initiative, participants must select high-quality courses, and in July 2022 five polytechnics signed an MOU with NTUC.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David
sentences.text: While there have been developments such as the appointment of the Institute of Adult Learning (IAL) appointed by SkillsFuture Singapore, to lead the national Innovative Learning 2.0 initiative, there must also be careful selection of high-quality courses by participants so that learning becomes meaningful.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David
sentences.text: I believe in July 2022, the five polytechnics signed a Memorandum of Understanding with NTUC through to elevate the quality of training and better support adult learners to adapt to the changing needs of the economy.

sections.label: Continuing education and Jobs-Skills Integrators
sections.summary: MOE is asked for an update on continuing education initiatives and how to build resilient adult learners, noting Jobs-Skills Integrators mentioned by Lawrence Wong in his Budget speech.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David
sentences.text: Can MOE provide an update on the initiatives to support continuing education, and additionally, how can we continue to build, develop, and support resilient adult learners who can be agile amidst the unpredictable economic and job environment?

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David
sentences.text: Recently, Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister Lawrence Wong mentioned Jobs-Skills Integrators in his Budget speech.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David
sentences.text: I understand that these Jobs-Skills Integrators are institutions which ensure training will improve employment and earnings prospects by working with industry, training and job placement partners.

sections.label: SSG-supported company participation
sections.summary: About 20,000 companies participated in SSG-supported programmes last year, 96% SMEs, and since 2020 about 16,000 companies used SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: Last year, about 20,000 companies participated in and benefitted from SSG-supported programmes; 96% of these were SMEs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: Since 2020, about 16,000 companies have tapped on SkillsFuture Entreprise Credit, a one-off $10,000 credit per firm, to send their employees for SSG-supported training programmes.

sections.label: NACE company support in 2022
sections.summary: In 2022, NACE supported close to 500 companies, of which 80% were SMEs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: In 2022, NACE supported close to 500 companies, of which 80% were SMEs.

sections.label: Jobs-Skills Integrator pilot sectors
sections.summary: SSG with Workforce Singapore, Enterprise Singapore and EDB will pilot Jobs-Skills Integrator in precision engineering, wholesale trade and retail, starting with precision engineering led by NYP's School of Engineering.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: SSG, together with Workforce Singapore, Enterprise Singapore and the Economic Development Board, will pilot Jobs-Skills Integrator (JSIT) in three sectors – precision engineering, wholesale trade and retail.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: Mr Darryl David and Mr Sharael Taha, as well as many others, asked for details of the JSIT pilot.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: We will start the pilot in the precision engineering (PE) sector, with Nanyang Polytechnic's (NYP) School of Engineering leading the effort.

sections.label: SGUnited programmes job placement
sections.summary: More than 60% of nearly 20,000 SGUnited Skills and Mid-Career Pathways trainees were placed in jobs within six months of course completion.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: Among the close to 20,000 individuals who completed the SGUnited Skills and the SGUnited Mid-Career Pathways – Company Training programmes, more than 60% were successfully placed in jobs within six months of course completion.

sections.label: Course fee subsidy and SkillsFuture Credit
sections.summary: SSG's course fee subsidy cut the full course fee from over $5,000 to about $600, and Choon Mei paid nothing as SkillsFuture Credit covered it.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: SSG's course fee subsidy reduced the full course fee from more than $5,000 to about $600, and Choon Mei did not have to pay any money out of her pocket as she could use her SkillsFuture Credit to pay for the course fee.

sections.label: Highest subsidy tier by end-2024
sections.summary: By end-2024 SSG will give the highest subsidy tier of 70% of course fees for programmes delivering strong manpower outcomes in employment and career progression.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: By end-2024 when the transition is completed, SSG will provide the highest tier of subsidies at 70% of course fees for programmes that deliver strong manpower outcomes, in terms of securing employment and career progression.

sections.label: Subsidies cease for non-certifiable courses
sections.summary: SSG will stop providing course fee subsidies to non-certifiable courses, including self-improvement courses.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: SSG will cease to provide course fee subsidies to non-certifiable courses, including self-improvement courses.

sections.label: Government CET spending nearly doubled
sections.summary: Government spending on CET nearly doubled since the SkillsFuture movement launched, from around $0.5 billion in FY2016 to $0.9 billion in FY2022.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: Government spending on CET has nearly doubled since the launch of the SkillsFuture movement, from around $0.5 billion in FY2016, to $0.9 billion in FY2022.

sections.label: Work-Study Programmes employment survey
sections.summary: The annual SkillsFuture Work-Study Programmes survey consistently showed more than 90% of trainees were employed within six months after completing the programme.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: For example, our annual survey on SkillsFuture Work-Study Programmes consistently showed that more than 90% of the trainees were employed within six months after completing the programme.

sections.label: Jobs-Skills Integrators appointment
sections.summary: Certain organisations will be designated as Jobs-Skills Integrators, starting with Nanyang Polytechnic for Precision Engineering.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: In some industries, we will designate certain organisations as Jobs-Skills Integrators (JSIT).

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: We will first appoint Nanyang Polytechnic as JSIT for the Precision Engineering industry.

sections.label: International schools in ASEAN cities
sections.summary: Funding international schools in ASEAN capitals depends on a critical mass of Singaporean children and parents' curriculum preferences.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: Assoc Prof Jamus Lim suggested funding and subsidising international schools in major ASEAN capital cities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: We have set up a Singapore International School in Hong Kong, whether we will do so in other cities, depends on whether there is a critical mass of schooling age Singaporean children who are concentrated in an area and whether their parents want to put them through the Singapore curriculum or prefer other options.

sections.label: Student's Pass applications
sections.summary: Foreign students accepted by EduTrust-certified institutions for full-time courses can apply for a Student's Pass through ICA's eService.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: Today, foreign students who are accepted by an EduTrust-certified institution to pursue full-time courses in Singapore can apply for a Student's Pass through ICA's eService.

sections.label: Food sustainability focus
sections.summary: In 2023, the focus will be on food sustainability.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: In 2023, our focus will be on food sustainability.
